newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev trades steady at 1,570-1,573 to dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev trades steady at 1,570-1,573 to dlr.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev steadied at 1,570-1,573 per dollar at mid-morning from the opening's 1,560-1,580, as investors eyed lev-denominated investments, dealers said.
"Foreign currency supply tops demand as investors are opting for lev-denominated instruments in anticipation of a stable lev in the next few weeks under the new government," one dealer said.
Some foreign currency sales for profit taking also supported the lev, traders said.
A new reformist government, pledging to continue the financial stabilisation policies of the interim cabinet, was voted in office by parliament on Wednesday.
The longer value date of today's spot deals was not seen pressuring the lev this morning so far. The value date falls on Tuesday because banks in the U.S. would be closed on Monday for Memorial Day.

The longer value date leaves room for a lev dip by 2.0-2.5 (levs) to the dollar daily until Tuesday due to the large spread between interest rates on lev- and dollar-denominated investments, traders said.

The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) might decide to cut its main interest rate on Thursday because yields on one- and four-week discount T-bills sold since last Friday have been lower than in the previous week, dealers said.
The BNB main interest is now set at 4.29 percent monthly.
"A rate cut might trigger some dollar shortcovering but the central bank is expected to intervene if pressure builds up on the lev," another dealer said.

The BNB usually adjusts its main rate each Thursday to the weighted average monthly yield of the one- and four-week discount T-bills sold from Friday through Thursday. The adjusted main rate usually goes in force from Monday.

Yields to maturity on one- and four-week T-bills sold between Friday and Wednesday stood at 0.41-0.51 percent and 3.55-3.82 percent respectively, down from 0.58-0.82 percent and 3.84-4.68 percent in the week May 9-15. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
